overview: Make the PoC safer and easier to reason about by (1) explicitly separating current vs target architecture docs, and (2) shipping P0 guardrails for object-store signed URL verification and ingest resource caps.
goals: Make docs explicitly separate current PoC behavior from target architecture.
Make signature verification safe-by-default (expiry enforced inside verifySignature).
Add ingest hard caps and persist honest extraction method metadata.
nonGoals: Implement OCR/layout providers and geometry-backed citations.
Replace runtime DDL with migrations (separate slice).
successMetrics: Architecture docs no longer imply unimplemented WDK/OCR/RAG behavior.
Expired signatures cannot be accepted even if a caller forgets an explicit expiry check.
Ingest failures are bounded and safe (no unbounded DB writes from pathological PDFs).
openQuestions: Should ingest caps be env-configurable (e.g. INGEST_MAX_PAGES) for demos, or kept as constants until migrations/durable jobs land?
Do we want to rename ocr_status to extraction_status in a later migration slice?

stack.objectStore: Local filesystem object store (tmp/object-store) with signed URL headers

stories.title: Signed URL verification is safe-by-default
stories.description: As an operator, I want signed URL verification to fail on expired signatures by default so that callers cannot accidentally accept expired URLs.
acceptanceCriteria: verifySignature() returns false when expiresAtMs is invalid or non-finite.
verifySignature() returns false when expiresAtMs < Date.now() even if the HMAC matches (example: expired URL).
Existing signed URL flows still work when expiresAtMs is valid and not expired (upload/render/download).
Negative case: a route that only calls verifySignature() (no explicit expiry check) still rejects expired signatures.

stories.title: Dev signing secret fallback is explicit opt-in
stories.description: As a developer, I want object-store signing to fail closed unless explicitly configured so that misconfigured deployments do not silently change the auth model.
acceptanceCriteria: If OBJECT_STORE_SIGNING_SECRET is unset: in non-development, signing throws OBJECT_STORE_SIGNING_SECRET_MISSING.
If OBJECT_STORE_SIGNING_SECRET is unset: in development, signing throws unless ALLOW_DEV_OBJECT_STORE_SECRET=1 (example: local dev misconfig gives actionable error).
If ALLOW_DEV_OBJECT_STORE_SECRET=1 in development, the dev fallback secret is used and signed URL flows work.
Negative case: NODE_ENV=development alone does not enable the fallback.

stories.title: Ingest is capped and extraction method is recorded
stories.description: As an operator, I want ingest to have hard caps and honest extraction metadata so the server remains stable and we do not misrepresent OCR/geometry guarantees.
acceptanceCriteria: If a PDF has more than MAX_PAGES, ingest fails early with a safe error code and the document becomes failed (example: oversized PDF).
Per-page extracted text is truncated to MAX_TEXT_CHARS_PER_PAGE and does not exceed it in document_pages.text or chunks.text.
documents.metadata_json.extraction_method is set to "pdfjs" for this ingest path.
document_pages.layout_json continues to set source="pdfjs" and has_geometry=false.
Negative case: a pathological PDF does not result in unbounded DB writes or huge per-page text rows.

stories.title: Architecture docs are explicit about current vs target
stories.description: As a contributor, I want architecture docs to explicitly separate current PoC behavior from target architecture so I can reason correctly when making changes.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/03-architecture/* includes an upfront note linking to a "Current PoC runtime" doc.
docs/03-architecture/10_system_architecture.md does not imply WDK/OCR/retrieve/draft/lock are already implemented without qualification.
docs/03-architecture/40_rag_and_agents.md clearly marks OCR/layout and retrieve/draft/lock as target and documents current fixture-backed behavior.
